newsitem.title: GERMANY: Albanian Airlines to launch Germany flights May 9.
newsitem.headline: Albanian Airlines to launch Germany flights May 9.

text.p: Albanian Airlines will start scheduled flights to Germany from May 9, a senior official said.
Mohammad Shamim, the airline's Germany general manager, said the Albanian national carrier will fly twice a week from Tirana to Frankfurt with a leased 76-seat, Soviet-built Tupolev 134.

Albanian Airlines dropped its four weekly Airbus A320 flights to Munich last year because of poor load factors, Shamim said in a Reuters interview. The A320 was on lease from Egyptair /Kuwait Airways -owned Shorouk Air.
"We are starting with two flights and will slowly build it up. We want to see how the German market develops with the ethnic traffic," he said.
Shamim noted that Deutsche Lufthansa AG was planning to increase its present four times a week service on the route to daily flights.

Albanian Airlines also aimed to target the three million Albanians in the United States and had signed interline ticket agreements with several airlines to transfer passengers to and from transatlantic flights at Frankfurt, he added.
Albanian Airlines expected to carry very little air cargo from Germany due to the small aircraft capacity, Shamim said.
The carrier's Germany cargo general sales agent is Frankfurt-based Aerotrans Luftfahrtagentur, he added.
-Paul Needham, Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706; Fax: 5017
